rationale: PINS THE MODULE LEAF OF A DECLARATION FILE (VERIFY_TS10). `imports` and `exports` edges are sourced from the module, and `moduleLeafName()` was `path.basename(file, path.extname(file))`. `path.extname("env.d.ts")` is `.ts`, so the leaf came out `env.d` while TypeScript — and every consumer that joins these edges — calls that module `env`. Measured by script/m14/ts-production-drop.mjs on element-plus: 368 imports+exports edges across 3 of its 8 .d.ts files were sourced from `env.d` / `components.d` / `index.d`, and a run of the lane's own imports/exports oracle against the same corpus disagreed with the analyzer on 365 of them for that reason alone. Every assertion here is about the SOURCE half of an edge; the target half is pinned by the imports/exports audit (imports 99.9% covered, exports 100.0%, 0 unexplained over a 150-file draw). The two forbid rows are the defect itself and they are load-bearing: with only the expect rows present, a fix that stopped emitting these edges would pass this fixture. 2026-10-18: the `export * from "./reexport"` dependency row now exists (re-export emission landed); the count pin moved 2 -> 3 for that row. Every assertion is still about the SOURCE half, and the source of the new row is the same module STEM. 2026-10-18: `export declare function build()` now emits its exports row (ambient-wrapper form) — exports count pin 1 -> 2. The module-leaf assertions are unchanged; every row is still about the SOURCE half.
